subject: PD brief 3 – 10 Nov 2026: 50 papers, 3 to dig into

synthesis.intro: These 8 days were dominated by cardiac arrest — community responder systems, ECPR outcomes and resuscitation detail — alongside a solid cluster of workforce wellbeing and paediatric care. Several studies support what crews already do, rather than asking for change.
synthesis.discussion: If trained community responders are rarely dispatched and a big prevention programme didn't move survival, is our effort on out-of-hospital arrest best spent on systems — or on what happens in the first five minutes on scene?

lessons.text: Layperson naloxone preceded nearly a third of overdose activations and was linked with less EMS naloxone and slightly fewer transports, without more airway attempts or arrests — a reason to keep encouraging bystander administration while staying alert that a lower transport rate can mean refusal rather than recovery.

Prehospital fentanyl in over 1,500 children showed rare serious adverse effects (bradycardia and respiratory depression each 0.7%) and no antidote use, supporting current cautious paediatric opioid practice — though most kids were still in pain on arrival, so adequate dosing matters as much as safety.

Paramedics counting drip rates varied by up to 45% from target in simulation, with whole-number rates and 1 gtt/s targets markedly more accurate — worth remembering whenever a counted drip is your only option and the rate genuinely matters.

Most registered community first responders were trained and felt prepared, yet only 15% had ever been dispatched — a prompt to consider whether your local responder scheme is actually activating the people it has signed up.

Mainstream and sidestream capnography gave ETCO2 values differing by around 4 mmHg on average while tracking trends almost identically — reassuring for trend-based decisions, but absolute numbers aren't interchangeable between devices.

deep_dives.why: A large cluster-randomised trial found no survival benefit from a community arrest programme, while a separate trial showed smart alerting beat a small fixed radius but offered nothing over simply widening it — together they challenge assumptions about where responder investment pays off.
questions: If a well-resourced community programme didn't shift survival at all, what would need to be different about a local version for it to work?
Does your experience of first responder arrivals on arrest calls match the finding that a wide radius performs as well as clever alerting?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare how the large trial bundled its four components with what your local responder scheme actually delivers, and consider whether the low dispatch rates reported in the survey could explain why trained volunteers aren't translating into earlier CPR.

deep_dives.why: Three studies this period describe ECPR selection, survival and life afterwards — including doubled survival in a nationwide comparison and detailed long-term follow-up showing most survivors live with good neurology. As Australian ECPR pathways expand, crews increasingly transport patients these numbers describe.
questions: The Dutch comparison was not randomised — how much of the doubled survival could be patient selection rather than the intervention?
Long-term follow-up found poor sleep and caregiver anxiety common among survivors: does your handover include what families should expect after discharge?
deep_dives.ideas: Look at how each study defined 'refractory' OHCA and who was excluded, and consider where those thresholds sit against the eligibility criteria in your local ECPR or cardiac arrest pathway.

deep_dives.topic: Violence and sleep in the prehospital workforce
deep_dives.why: A qualitative study showed violence follows staff home and that organisational support feels thin, a survey tied long shifts and consecutive deployments to broken sleep, and a review found most prehospital staff report career violence — a pattern relevant to every crew, not just those who report incidents.
questions: Which of the coping strategies described — communication, de-escalation, situational awareness, peer support — does your crew use deliberately rather than by accident?
What does 'insufficient organisational support' look like in your own service after a violent job?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the Italian participants' experiences of microaggressions with what gets formally reported as violence locally, and consider how sleep findings from disaster deployment might or might not apply to your routine roster.

papers.title: Prehospital stroke triage: high under- and overtriage rates
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre quality-control study
papers.n: 1,071 patients with suspected acute ischaemic stroke
papers.finding: 41% were eligible for reperfusion; EMS undertriage 21%, overtriage 63%; the physician-led call-team step reduced undertriage to 11% and overtriage to 57%

papers.title: Reported LOC didn't flag post-traumatic amnesia in ED
papers.design: Single-centre retrospective cohort
papers.n: 6,259 adults presenting to ED with head injury
papers.finding: 91.8% passed the A-WPTAS; PTA was more frequent with GCS 13–14, in male patients, after low falls and after hours, but pass rates were similar with documented LOC (90.6%) and without (92%, p=0.13)

papers.title: Wearables detecting cardiac arrest: systematic review
papers.design: Systematic review
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Abstract not yet available

papers.title: Predicting ground vs helicopter EMS travel times
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Model development and validation using open-source routing and historical travel times
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Best ground EMS models explained R² 0.79 (drive time to location) and 0.70 (to hospital) versus R² 0.46 and 0.38 for helicopter flight times; mean absolute percentage error 18–20% across all methods

papers.title: Mapping anti-violence measures for ambulance personnel
papers.design: Scoping review protocol (JBI methodology, PRISMA-ScR reporting)
papers.n: Literature from 2014 to May 2026 across five databases
papers.finding: Protocol only — no results yet; between 57% and 93% of prehospital responders report at least one episode of verbal or physical violence in their career

papers.title: EMS rarely suspects PE, but detection speeds CT
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre cohort, EMS protocols 2019-2024
papers.n: 171 EMS-transported patients with in-hospital confirmed PE, Bochum, Germany
papers.finding: PE correctly suspected prehospital in 9/171 (5.3%, 95% CI 2.8-9.7%); time to CTPA 2.1 vs 4.0 hours with detection (p<0.001); detection only in physician-staffed encounters (10.8% vs 0%, p=0.003); 22.5% diagnosed only after 24 hours

papers.title: Workplace violence follows prehospital staff home
papers.design: Qualitative interpretative study, semi-structured interviews, inductive content analysis
papers.n: 15 prehospital nurses and ambulance drivers, northeastern Italy
papers.finding: Three themes: 'Violence is taken home', 'Microaggressions: the invisible violence', and coping via communication, de-escalation, situational awareness and peer support; organisational support perceived as insufficient

papers.title: Paediatric transport ventilation: nCPAP first, transfers dominate
papers.design: Retrospective descriptive study of electronic records, 2023
papers.n: 1,548 ventilated under-5s among 61,775 paediatric/neonatal activations, Western Cape public EMS
papers.finding: Interfacility transfers 99.4%; respiratory distress 73.5%; nCPAP 66.5%, high-flow nasal cannula 14.5%, invasive ventilation 18.9%; high FiO2 (>0.6) documented in 11.6% of nCPAP cases

papers.title: AI in prehospital care: cautious optimism, thin validation
papers.design: Critical narrative review
papers.n: Not reported (narrative review)
papers.finding: Most credible near-term uses are bounded decision support in triage, early risk stratification, stroke pathways, operational forecasting and supervised documentation; field constrained by retrospective designs, limited external validation and workflow integration gaps

papers.title: Trained ChatGPT matched paramedics on triage scenarios
papers.design: Simulation-based comparative study, 100 Pre-KTAS scenarios × 30 independent repetitions
papers.n: 100 scenarios; trained and untrained LLM vs 10 active-duty 119 paramedics
papers.finding: Accuracy: trained LLM 0.81 vs paramedics 0.80 vs untrained LLM 0.69 (trained LLM and paramedics > untrained, p<.001); trained LLM lowest under-triage (6.1%) and highest sensitivity (0.95); paramedics highest specificity (0.96) and PPV (0.93)

papers.title: Remote reads of paramedic ultrasound held up in pilot
papers.design: Mixed-methods usability pilot, 4 physicians × 3 sessions × 3 device modalities
papers.n: 4 physicians, 4 clinical vignettes with lung and IVC clips
papers.finding: Chance-adjusted agreement: laptop 0.80, smartphone 0.72, tablet 0.68; observed agreement lung 80-83%, IVC 73-75%; SUS scores 76.5 laptop, 59.5 smartphone, 55.0 tablet

papers.title: What helps kids in pain in ambulances
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Realist evaluation (qualitative interviews, diaries, artwork + routine clinical records)
papers.n: 44 participants (21 ambulance clinicians, 14 parents/carers, 9 children/young people); 34,068 clinical records
papers.finding: Around 60% of children and young people needing an ambulance for a painful condition experience poor pain management; preparedness (education, training, exposure, experience) and compassionate person-centred care were the refined programme theory's central mechanisms

papers.title: M-DIRECT stroke triage scale revalidated
papers.design: Prospective observational cohort
papers.n: 1,950 prehospital code-stroke patients, urban network of 6.75 million
papers.finding: Sensitivity 77%, specificity 76%, AUC 0.768 for EVT; 58% of M-DIRECT-positive patients had LVO/MeVO and 50% underwent EVT; positive score independently associated with EVT (aOR 3.05, 95% CI 1.65–5.68); only 10% of EVT patients needed a secondary transfer

papers.title: Post-ROSC ST elevation tracks acute coronary occlusion
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre cohort
papers.n: 149 successfully resuscitated OHCA patients undergoing post-resuscitation angiography
papers.finding: ST elevation was associated with more impaired culprit-vessel flow and greater myocardial injury; patients without ST elevation more often had multivessel disease or chronic total occlusion; ST elevation was not independently associated with neurological outcome after adjustment for prehospital factors

papers.title: Two-thirds of ECPR survivors alive at five years
papers.design: Retrospective two-centre cohort (Minnesota, USA and Prague, Czechia)
papers.n: 728 ECPR patients, 211 discharged alive
papers.finding: 211/728 (29.0%) survived to discharge; 76.9% and 67.2% of hospital survivors were alive at 1 and 5 years; CPC 1–2 in 78.7% at discharge and above 93% among survivors beyond 1 year; five-year survival ranged from 91.6% (18–39 years) to 52.9% (>70 years)

papers.title: STEMI deaths now mostly prehospital
papers.design: Perspective/viewpoint article
papers.n: Not applicable
papers.finding: Five recommendations to shorten symptom onset to reperfusion: patient education, prehospital glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors or thrombolytics, rapid PCI access, and changes to prehospital care reimbursement

papers.title: Long wildfire shifts linked to broken sleep
papers.journal: Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine
papers.design: Cross-sectional survey
papers.n: 90 first responders
papers.finding: 24-hour shifts associated with 1.65 fewer total sleep hours (95% CI −2.45 to −0.84) and 1.93 fewer consecutive hours; four or more consecutive shifts and poorer working conditions also associated with shorter sleep; 83% reported poor or very poor sleep quality

papers.title: Turning HEMS debriefs into shared learning
papers.design: Qualitative descriptive study, four semi-structured focus groups
papers.n: 30 HEMS clinicians in 4 focus groups
papers.finding: Organisational learning was the global theme, organised into education (knowledge generation, engagement, incidental learning), accessibility (learning reaching staff who missed debriefs) and calibration (moderation and vetting of learning points)

papers.title: US Medicaid cuts threaten EMS funding
papers.design: Policy commentary
papers.n: Not applicable
papers.finding: H.R. 1 and subsequent CMS rules are expected to place financial strain on local EMS systems already struggling with inadequate reimbursement

papers.title: Electrical capture uncommon in prehospital transcutaneous pacing
papers.design: Retrospective cohort with continuous ECG review
papers.n: 56 patients who received prehospital transcutaneous pacing
papers.finding: Electrical capture in 18/56 (32%); among capturers, complete capture occurred only 27.2% of pacing time; median SBP change +22 mmHg with capture vs 0 mmHg without (p=0.031); clinician-verbalised pulse coincided with electrical capture in only 4/26 (15%) instances

papers.title: Counted drip rates vary widely between paramedics
papers.design: Controlled laboratory simulation
papers.n: 55 paramedics, nine drip rates each
papers.finding: Overall inaccuracy ranged from -45.3% to +5.8%; imprecision was primarily human; 1 gtt/s targets more accurate than all others (absolute error 31.1% vs 48.5%); whole-number rates more accurate than fractional (40.7% vs 54.1%)

papers.title: Military prehospital transfusion often outside guideline criteria
papers.design: Multicentre retrospective observational study
papers.n: 206 trauma casualties evacuated, 64 transfused with 89 blood products
papers.finding: Meeting transfusion criteria was associated with requiring transfusion (RR 3.20, 95% CI 2.29–4.47); 65% of transfused patients did not meet criteria; median transfusion rate 25 mL/min

papers.title: START triage knowledge unrelated to student decision styles
papers.journal: Disaster Medicine and Public Health Preparedness
papers.design: Cross-sectional questionnaire study
papers.n: 121 paramedic students
papers.finding: Mean START knowledge score 69.99 ± 14.76; no significant association with intolerance of uncertainty or any decision-making style subscale

papers.title: 2026 ILCOR resuscitation consensus published
papers.design: International consensus statement (systematic evidence review)
papers.n: 191 authors across six ILCOR task forces
papers.finding: Abstract not yet available; the full CoSTR covers basic life support, advanced life support, paediatric life support, neonatal life support, education/implementation/teams and first aid.

papers.title: Layperson naloxone linked to fewer EMS interventions
papers.design: Cross-sectional analysis of a national EMS registry
papers.n: 26,087 EMS activations for opioid overdose (adults 16 and over)
papers.finding: Layperson naloxone preceded 30.7% of activations; any subsequent EMS naloxone 24.4% vs 34.8% (aOR 0.73, 95% CI 0.68–0.78) and transport 79.4% vs 84.4% (aOR 0.78, 95% CI 0.73–0.84); advanced airway attempts (1.6% vs 1.4%) and cardiac arrest (6.6% vs 6.0%) uncommon in both groups.

papers.title: Physiology-based traumatic shock pathway rolled out
papers.design: Single-centre quality-improvement implementation study with pre/post staff surveys
papers.n: 3,667 major trauma patients, of whom 324 (8.8%) met shocked trauma criteria
papers.finding: Shocked patients had markedly higher ED mortality (6.8% vs 0.4%); favourable ratings of trauma bay equipment rose from about one-quarter to 87.0%, with 85.2–88.9% favourability for timely life-saving interventions, pathway embedding and role confidence.

papers.title: Long-term life after ECPR for cardiac arrest
papers.design: Single-centre cohort with long-term multidimensional follow-up
papers.n: 406 ECPR-treated patients; 17 survivors and 19 caregivers formally assessed
papers.finding: 63/406 (16%) discharged alive; at median 3.1 years 61% were alive, 82% with favourable neurology, and only 1.7% of all treated were alive with poor neurology; mild cognitive impairment in 6/16 survivors, poor sleep in 10/17, anxiety symptoms more common in caregivers (6/18 vs 1/17).

papers.title: First consensus on TBI in first responders
papers.journal: The Journal of Head Trauma Rehabilitation
papers.design: Consensus statement (modified Delphi, two voting rounds)
papers.n: 52 panel members; 28 final recommendations
papers.finding: 27 of 29 preliminary statements reached consensus in round 1 and all 28 final recommendations reached the 80% threshold in round 2, across six domains from injury risk and reporting to workplace policy.

papers.title: Stroke triage app adopted but not embedded
papers.design: Sequential mixed-methods implementation evaluation (usage data, survey, interviews)
papers.n: 246 paramedics with app accounts; 76 surveyed, 9 interviewed
papers.finding: Median 120 triages/month (IQR 107–131) and median 7 uses per paramedic (IQR 3–13); the app was well accepted and supported structured neurological assessment, but clinical urgency, poor workflow integration and limited perceived added value hampered routine use.

papers.title: FAST feasible in a moving ambulance (manikin)
papers.design: Prospective observational simulation pilot with non-inferiority analysis
papers.n: 20 Emergency Life-Saving Technicians, three speed conditions
papers.finding: Mean Task-Specific Checklist scores 23.4 stationary, 23.4 at 15 km/h and 23.7 at 30 km/h (of 24); non-inferiority met at both speeds, and specialist physicians could review transmitted images.

papers.title: Hoisted paramedic beat antenna in avalanche search
papers.design: Dual randomised experimental field trial with an operational SAR helicopter crew
papers.n: 25 trial runs (13 antenna, 12 hoist) over three days, six buried transceivers
papers.finding: Hoist search cut time to transceiver found by 143 seconds (95% CI 113–172, p<0.001), time to optimal signal by 29 seconds and time to paramedic on ground by 124 seconds.

papers.title: Low-cost 3D-printed skin tear trainer for paramedics
papers.design: Technical report with iterative prototyping and acceptability assessment
papers.n: 14 type 1 task trainers assessed with paramedic learners
papers.finding: Perceived self-efficacy 4.68/5, realism 4.64/5 and educational value 4.85/5; each unit took 20–30 minutes of active fabrication plus 80–90 minutes curing.

papers.title: Paediatric prehospital fentanyl: serious adverse effects rare
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Retrospective register-based cohort with medical record review
papers.n: 1,531 children aged 0–14 given prehospital opioids, Denmark 2017–2022
papers.finding: 15.1% had at least one clinical sign compatible with opioid-related adverse effects; bradycardia 0.7%, respiratory depression 0.7%; no opioid antidote given; 63.6% in pain at arrival and 51% received further in-hospital analgesia.

papers.title: CARE framework for traumatic cardiac arrest
papers.design: Framework / consensus-style paper
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Not reported — abstract not yet available.

papers.title: Forecast: prehospital transfusion growth and HDFN risk
papers.design: Forecasting model (regression on US transfusion trends, 500 instantiations per model)
papers.n: 779 females of childbearing potential projected to receive prehospital transfusion in the US in 2029
papers.finding: One HDFN case forecast every 0.5–20 years depending on region and model (base case: 0.5 years in the South, 20.0 in the Northeast).

papers.title: First responders notifying schools after child trauma
papers.design: Mixed-methods first-year implementation evaluation (training, notification process, surveys, qualitative interviews)
papers.n: 75 school staff and 64 first responders, one Mississippi school district
papers.finding: Significant gains in school staff trauma-informed attitudes; greater first-responder training exposure linked with lower burnout; disciplinary referrals decreased overall while in-school suspensions increased; attendance stable.

papers.title: Layperson CPR: pocket mask versus face shield
papers.design: Randomised crossover simulation study
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Not reported — abstract not yet available.

papers.title: Mainstream and sidestream capnography give different ETCO2
papers.design: Retrospective device-comparison analysis of synchronized capnography waveforms
papers.n: 23 OHCA recordings (3,460 paired ventilations)
papers.finding: Mainstream ETCO2 bias +3.94 mmHg vs sidestream (limits of agreement -3.21 to 11.09 mmHg, proportional bias 0.0746); trends matched (-1.44 vs -1.41 mmHg/min, p=0.93); abrupt rises >=10 mmHg co-detected in 7/8 and drops in 10/15

papers.title: Community first responders trained but rarely dispatched
papers.design: Multicentre cross-sectional survey (two regions, pre-implementation)
papers.n: 2,704 respondents of 14,141 registered first responders (19.1%)
papers.finding: 84.3% had CPR training within two years and 97.3% felt prepared (both associated with healthcare/emergency background and recent training, p<0.001), yet only 15.1% had ever been dispatched, 2.8% arrived before EMS and 1.9% performed CPR

papers.title: Mapping chest pain risk tools in ambulance care
papers.design: Scoping review (JBI methodology, PRISMA-ScR)
papers.n: 27 articles, 8 risk-stratification tools
papers.finding: Eight chest-pain risk-stratification tools were used or trialled in ambulance settings; HEART and its derivatives were the most frequently studied, with performance varying across settings and validation for ambulance use incomplete

papers.title: AI in cardiac arrest: oversight may be symbolic
papers.design: Conceptual/policy analysis (no empirical data)
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: No empirical data — proposes five policy measures including ecological trialling, designed-in explainability, defined escalation triggers and authority, and protection for justified deviation from AI recommendations

papers.title: Smart first-responder alerting vs fixed-radius alerts in OHCA
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.design: Prospective randomised three-arm trial
papers.n: 823 activations, 1482 dispatched community first responders
papers.finding: CFR arrived before EMS in 58% (smart alerting), 57% (2500 m) and 31% (600 m); smart alerting vs 600 m risk difference +26.8% (95% CI 18.6–34.4), vs 2500 m +1.2% (95% CI −7.0 to +9.3, p=0.80)

papers.title: PEEP during CPR linked with more ROSC
papers.journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Single-centre retrospective cohort with continuous intratracheal pressure monitoring, physician-staffed EMS
papers.n: 362 intubated adults with OHCA
papers.finding: Adjusted OR for ROSC with mechanical ventilation using PEEP 1.58 (95% CI 1.01–2.50, p=0.048); unadjusted OR for survival to hospital discharge 2.22 (95% CI 1.03–4.78)

papers.title: Ultrasound added to stroke scales for LVO triage
papers.design: Exploratory secondary analysis of a 20-patient portable ultrasound device trial
papers.n: 20 patients with acute ischaemic stroke
papers.finding: Combining brain perfusion ultrasound with prehospital stroke scales shifted sensitivity and negative predictive value higher and reclassified all patients misdiagnosed by either method alone; three prehospital-ICH false positives showed severe perfusion deficits suggesting LVO

papers.title: Prehospital ECPR linked to doubled arrest survival
papers.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
papers.design: Nationwide nonrandomised comparative cohort (OnScene, Netherlands)
papers.n: 231 adults ≤ 50 with refractory OHCA (144 ECPR-capable HEMS vs 87 conventional)
papers.finding: Survival to discharge 40% with ECPR vs 20% without (OR 2.72, 95% CI 1.59–4.66); favourable neurological outcome at 6 months 36% vs 13% (OR 4.22, 95% CI 2.82–6.32); 32 adverse events with ECPR vs 11

papers.title: Big community arrest programme didn't change survival
papers.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
papers.design: Registry-based cluster-randomised trial (CARES registry, North Carolina)
papers.n: 22,459 adults with OHCA across 55 county clusters
papers.finding: Survival to discharge with good neurological outcome 9.0% (intervention) vs 9.4% (usual care), adjusted OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.75–1.26, P = 0.80

papers.title: Intubation linked to more ROSC in OHCA registry
papers.design: Retrospective registry cohort with propensity-score matching
papers.n: 6,162 adults with non-traumatic OHCA (1,448 intubated vs 4,714 basic airway)
papers.finding: ROSC 21.1% with intubation vs 3.8% with basic airway (multivariable OR 7.61, propensity-matched OR 6.33); the unadjusted association was not significant in the shockable-rhythm stratum

papers.title: Whole blood vs components: mixed mortality, lower transfusion needs
papers.journal: International Journal of Medicine in Developing Countries
papers.design: Systematic review (PRISMA 2020, ROBINS-I) of comparative studies
papers.n: 22 comparative studies, about 95,000 trauma patients
papers.finding: Survival benefit with whole blood in some studies — hypotensive patients (aOR 0.72 for SBP<90), penetrating injury (RR 0.36), geriatric (OR 0.60) — but no difference in others including one randomised trial; transfusion requirements consistently lower with whole blood; VTE risk lower (OR 0.70)

papers.title: Heat alerts eased heat-dispatch risk but demand still grew
papers.design: Two-stage distributed lag nonlinear model time-series analysis across 47 prefectures
papers.n: 577,027 heat-related ambulance dispatches, Japan 2015–2023
papers.finding: At the 95th WBGT percentile the pooled cumulative relative risk fell from 10.45 (2015–19) to 5.90 (2022–23), a 43.6% reduction; severe-case relative risks also declined while age 65+ became the strongest effect modifier; heat-attributable counts still rose 18.1%

papers.title: EMS students report obs/gyn training gaps
papers.design: Qualitative conventional content analysis, semi-structured interviews
papers.n: 14 EMS students and recent graduates, Iran
papers.finding: 1,532 codes distilled to six challenge categories: educational content and approaches, clinical education barriers, communication and cultural barriers, resource limitations, motivation and educational justice, and process management; higher-order category: disconnects between preparation and real-world demands
